_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for eat-stay-love-carcassonne, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Book the table, not just the room
items.summary: Good small restaurants fill early in high season.

items.title: Eat lunch like a local: the formule du jour
items.summary: A set menu at midday is often the best value.

items.title: Say bonjour before anything else
items.summary: In shops and cafés the greeting comes before the question. It changes the whole exchange.

items.title: Learn the market days
items.summary: In a small French town the week is organized around them. Ask at the tourist office or town hall.

items.title: Check opening hours before you set out
items.summary: Many places close at midday and on Sundays or Mondays.

items.title: Walk the old walls at the quiet end of the day
items.summary: Early morning and late evening show a place before and after the crowds.

items.title: Follow one canal or river path for a whole afternoon
items.summary: Take a picnic and no plan.

items.title: Taste one regional dish in three places and compare
items.summary: A small, delicious study of how a place cooks.

items.title: Météo-France
items.summary: The national weather service, with local forecasts and alerts.

items.title: SNCF Connect
items.summary: Plan and book trains across France.

items.title: Service-Public
items.summary: The official guide to French administration and procedures.

items.title: Join a local association
items.summary: Choirs, walking clubs and conversation groups are the fastest way into village life.

items.title: Volunteer at a village festival
items.summary: Festivals run on volunteers and neighbors welcome help.

items.title: Shop what is in season, then decide what to cook
items.summary: Start at the market, not the recipe. Seasonal food tastes better and costs less.

items.title: Salt in layers while you cook
items.summary: A pinch at each stage builds flavor. Salt only at the end and it just sits on top.

items.title: Cook a dish from a region you have never visited
items.summary: Read about where it comes from first, then cook it, then eat it slowly.

items.title: Host a potluck where every dish has a story
items.summary: Everyone brings a dish and says why it matters to them.

items.title: Paprika
items.summary: Save recipes from the web, plan meals and build shopping lists.

items.title: Vivino
items.summary: Scan a wine label to see ratings and tasting notes.

items.title: Take a class from a local cook
items.summary: A few hours with a home cook teaches more than a shelf of books.
